passages.text: Now a man named Ananias, together with his wife Sapphira, also sold a piece of property.
passages.sermon: Ananias was a man.\r\nHis wife was Sapphira.\r\nAnanias and Sapphira sold a piece of property.
passages.original: Ἀνὴρ δέ τις Ἁνανίας ὀνόματι σὺν Σαπφίρῃ τῇ γυναικὶ αὐτοῦ ἐπώλησεν κτῆμα

passages.text: With his wife’s full knowledge, he kept back some of the proceeds for himself, but brought a portion and laid it at the apostles’ feet.
passages.sermon:
Ananias was a man.
Sapphira was his wife.
Ananias sold a piece of property.
Sapphira knew what he did.
Ananias kept part of the money for himself.
He brought only a portion of the money.
He laid this portion at the apostles’ feet.
passages.original: καὶ ἐνοσφίσατο ἀπὸ τῆς τιμῆς συνειδυίης καὶ τῆς γυναικός καὶ ἐνέγκας μέρος τι παρὰ τοὺς πόδας τῶν ἀποστόλων ἔθηκεν

passages.text: Then Peter said, “Ananias, how is it that Satan has filled your heart to lie to the Holy Spirit and withhold some of the proceeds from the land?
passages.sermon:
Peter was an apostle of Jesus Christ.
Peter spoke to Ananias.
Peter said, “Ananias, why has Satan filled your heart?”
Satan is the enemy of God.
Satan causes people to do evil.
Peter said, “You have lied to the Holy Spirit.”
The Holy Spirit is God’s Spirit.
Peter said, “You kept back part of the money from the land.”
Ananias sold a piece of property.
Ananias did not give all the money to the apostles.
Ananias kept some of the money for himself.
Peter asked why Ananias did this.
passages.original: Εἶπεν δὲ ὁ Πέτρος Ἁνανία διὰ τί ἐπλήρωσεν ὁ Σατανᾶς τὴν καρδίαν σου ψεύσασθαί σε τὸ Πνεῦμα τὸ Ἅγιον καὶ νοσφίσασθαι ἀπὸ τῆς τιμῆς τοῦ χωρίου

passages.text: Did it not belong to you before it was sold? And after it was sold, was it not at your disposal? How could you conceive such a deed in your heart? You have not lied to men, but to God!”
passages.sermon:
Peter spoke to Ananias.
Peter was an apostle of Jesus Christ.
Peter said, “Ananias, the land belonged to you before you sold it.
After you sold the land, the money was still under your control.
You decided in your heart to do this thing.
You have not lied to people.
You have lied to God.”
passages.original: οὐχὶ μένον σοὶ ἔμενεν καὶ πραθὲν ἐν τῇ σῇ ἐξουσίᾳ ὑπῆρχεν τί ὅτι ἔθου ἐν τῇ καρδίᾳ σου τὸ πρᾶγμα τοῦτο οὐκ ἐψεύσω ἀνθρώποις ἀλλὰ τῷ Θεῷ

passages.text: On hearing these words, Ananias fell down and died. And great fear came over all who heard what had happened.
passages.sermon:
Ananias heard these words from Peter.
Ananias fell down.
Ananias died.
Everyone who heard about this became very afraid.
passages.original: Ἀκούων δὲ ὁ Ἁνανίας τοὺς λόγους τούτους πεσὼν ἐξέψυξεν καὶ ἐγένετο φόβος μέγας ἐπὶ πάντας τοὺς ἀκούοντας

passages.text: Then the young men stepped forward, wrapped up his body, and carried him out and buried him.
passages.sermon:
The young men stood up.
They wrapped up Ananias’s body.
They carried his body out.
They buried him.
passages.original: ἀναστάντες δὲ οἱ νεώτεροι συνέστειλαν αὐτὸν καὶ ἐξενέγκαντες ἔθαψαν

passages.text: About three hours later his wife also came in, unaware of what had happened.
passages.sermon: About three hours passed.\r\nAnanias’s wife came in.\r\nShe did not know what had happened.
passages.original: Ἐγένετο δὲ ὡς ὡρῶν τριῶν διάστημα καὶ ἡ γυνὴ αὐτοῦ μὴ εἰδυῖα τὸ γεγονὸς εἰσῆλθεν

passages.text: “Tell me,” said Peter, “is this the price you and your husband got for the land?” “Yes,” she answered, “that is the price.”
passages.sermon:
Peter spoke to her.
Peter was one of Jesus’ apostles.
Peter said, “Tell me the truth.”
Peter asked, “Did you and your husband sell the land for this amount?”
She answered Peter.
She said, “Yes, that is the price.”
passages.original: ἀπεκρίθη δὲ πρὸς αὐτὴν Πέτρος Εἰπέ μοι εἰ τοσούτου τὸ χωρίον ἀπέδοσθε Ἡ δὲ εἶπεν Ναί τοσούτου

passages.text: “How could you agree to test the Spirit of the Lord?” Peter replied. “Look, the feet of the men who buried your husband are at the door, and they will carry you out also.”
passages.sermon:
Peter spoke to her.
Peter was an apostle and a leader in the early church.
He said, “Why did you and your husband agree to test the Spirit of the Lord?”
He said, “Look. The men who buried your husband are at the door.”
He said, “They will carry you out also.”
passages.original: Ὁ δὲ Πέτρος πρὸς αὐτήν Τί ὅτι συνεφωνήθη ὑμῖν πειράσαι τὸ Πνεῦμα Κυρίου ἰδοὺ οἱ πόδες τῶν θαψάντων τὸν ἄνδρα σου ἐπὶ τῇ θύρᾳ καὶ ἐξοίσουσίν σε

passages.text: At that instant she fell down at his feet and died. Then the young men came in and, finding her dead, carried her out and buried her beside her husband.
passages.sermon:
A woman stood before Peter.
She fell down at Peter’s feet immediately.
She died at that moment.
The young men entered the room.
They found her dead.
They carried her body out.
They buried her beside her husband.
passages.original: Ἔπεσεν δὲ παραχρῆμα πρὸς τοὺς πόδας αὐτοῦ καὶ ἐξέψυξεν εἰσελθόντες δὲ οἱ νεανίσκοι εὗρον αὐτὴν νεκράν καὶ ἐξενέγκαντες ἔθαψαν πρὸς τὸν ἄνδρα αὐτῆς

passages.text: And great fear came over the whole church and all who heard about these events.
passages.sermon:
The whole church heard about these events.
All the people who heard about these events felt fear.
Great fear came over the entire church.
Great fear came over everyone who heard these things.
passages.original: Καὶ ἐγένετο φόβος μέγας ἐφ’ ὅλην τὴν ἐκκλησίαν καὶ ἐπὶ πάντας τοὺς ἀκούοντας ταῦτα

passages.text: The apostles performed many signs and wonders among the people, and with one accord the believers gathered together in Solomon’s Colonnade.
passages.sermon:
The apostles performed many signs.
The apostles performed many wonders.
They did these things among the people.
All the believers gathered together.
They met with one accord.
They gathered in Solomon’s Colonnade.
passages.original: Διὰ δὲ τῶν χειρῶν τῶν ἀποστόλων ἐγίνετο σημεῖα καὶ τέρατα πολλὰ ἐν τῷ λαῷ καὶ ἦσαν ὁμοθυμαδὸν ἅπαντες ἐν τῇ στοᾷ Σολομῶντος

passages.text: Although the people regarded them highly, no one else dared to join them.
passages.sermon:
The people respected the apostles.
No one else dared to join the apostles.
The people honored the apostles.
passages.original: τῶν δὲ λοιπῶν οὐδεὶς ἐτόλμα κολλᾶσθαι αὐτοῖς ἀλλ’ ἐμεγάλυνεν αὐτοὺς ὁ λαός

passages.text: Yet more and more believers were brought to the Lord—large numbers of both men and women.
passages.sermon: Many people believed in the Lord.\r\nThese people included both men and women.\r\nThe number of believers grew larger and larger.
passages.original: μᾶλλον δὲ προσετίθεντο πιστεύοντες τῷ Κυρίῳ πλήθη ἀνδρῶν τε καὶ γυναικῶν

passages.text: As a result, people brought the sick into the streets and laid them on cots and mats, so that at least Peter’s shadow might fall on some of them as he passed by.
passages.sermon:
The apostles performed many signs and wonders.
People saw these miracles.
People believed God worked through the apostles.
People brought sick people into the streets.
They laid the sick on cots and mats.
They wanted Peter’s shadow to fall on some of the sick as he passed by.
They believed even Peter’s shadow could help the sick.
passages.original: ὥστε καὶ εἰς τὰς πλατείας ἐκφέρειν τοὺς ἀσθενεῖς καὶ τιθέναι ἐπὶ κλιναρίων καὶ κραβάττων ἵνα ἐρχομένου Πέτρου κἂν ἡ σκιὰ ἐπισκιάσῃ τινὶ αὐτῶν

passages.text: Crowds also gathered from the towns around Jerusalem, bringing the sick and those tormented by unclean spirits, and all of them were healed.
passages.sermon:
Many people lived in towns around Jerusalem.
Large crowds came from these towns.
They brought people who were sick.
They also brought people who suffered because of unclean spirits.
The apostles met these crowds.
The apostles healed every sick person.
The apostles freed all who were tormented by unclean spirits.
passages.original: συνήρχετο δὲ καὶ τὸ πλῆθος τῶν πέριξ πόλεων Ἰερουσαλήμ φέροντες ἀσθενεῖς καὶ ὀχλουμένους ὑπὸ πνευμάτων ἀκαθάρτων οἵτινες ἐθεραπεύοντο ἅπαντες

passages.text: Then the high priest and all his associates, who belonged to the party of the Sadducees, were filled with jealousy. They went out and arrested the apostles and put them in the public jail.
passages.sermon:
The high priest led a group of men.
These men belonged to the party of the Sadducees.
The high priest and his associates felt great jealousy.
They acted because of this jealousy.
They seized the apostles.
They arrested the apostles.
They put the apostles in the public jail.
passages.original: Ἀναστὰς δὲ ὁ ἀρχιερεὺς καὶ πάντες οἱ σὺν αὐτῷ ἡ οὖσα αἵρεσις τῶν Σαδδουκαίων ἐπλήσθησαν ζήλου καὶ ἐπέβαλον τὰς χεῖρας ἐπὶ τοὺς ἀποστόλους καὶ ἔθεντο αὐτοὺς ἐν τηρήσει δημοσίᾳ

passages.text: But during the night an angel of the Lord opened the doors of the jail and brought them out, saying, “Go, stand in the temple courts and tell the people the full message of this new life.”
passages.sermon:
An angel of the Lord came during the night.
The angel opened the doors of the jail.
The angel brought the apostles out of the jail.
The angel spoke to the apostles.
The angel said, “Go to the temple courts.
Stand there.
Speak to the people.
Tell them everything about this new life.”
passages.original: Ἄγγελος δὲ Κυρίου διὰ νυκτὸς ἤνοιξε τὰς θύρας τῆς φυλακῆς ἐξαγαγών τε αὐτοὺς εἶπεν Πορεύεσθε καὶ σταθέντες λαλεῖτε ἐν τῷ ἱερῷ τῷ λαῷ πάντα τὰ ῥήματα τῆς Ζωῆς ταύτης

passages.text: At daybreak the apostles entered the temple courts as they had been told and began to teach the people. When the high priest and his associates arrived, they convened the Sanhedrin—the full assembly of the elders of Israel—and sent to the jail for the apostles.
passages.sermon:
The apostles were followers of Jesus.
They listened to the angel’s command.
At daybreak, the apostles went into the temple courts.
They began to teach the people there.
The high priest was the leader of the Jewish religious authorities.
His associates were with him.
They arrived at the temple.
They called together the Sanhedrin.
The Sanhedrin was the full assembly of the elders of Israel.
The high priest and his associates sent men to the jail.
They wanted the apostles to be brought from the jail.
passages.original: Ἀκούσαντες δὲ εἰσῆλθον ὑπὸ τὸν ὄρθρον εἰς τὸ ἱερὸν καὶ ἐδίδασκον Παραγενόμενος δὲ ὁ ἀρχιερεὺς καὶ οἱ σὺν αὐτῷ συνεκάλεσαν τὸ συνέδριον καὶ πᾶσαν τὴν γερουσίαν τῶν υἱῶν Ἰσραήλ καὶ ἀπέστειλαν εἰς τὸ δεσμωτήριον ἀχθῆναι αὐτούς

passages.text: But on arriving at the jail, the officers did not find them there. So they returned with the report: “We found the jail securely locked, with the guards posted at the doors; but when we opened them, we found no one inside.”
passages.sermon:
The officers went to the jail.
They did not find the apostles inside.
The officers returned to the leaders.
They gave a report.
They said, “We found the jail locked very securely.
We saw the guards standing at the doors.
But when we opened the doors, we found no one inside.”
passages.original: οἱ δὲ παραγενόμενοι ὑπηρέται οὐχ εὗρον αὐτοὺς ἐν τῇ φυλακῇ ἀναστρέψαντες δὲ ἀπήγγειλαν λέγοντες ὅτι Τὸ δεσμωτήριον εὕρομεν κεκλεισμένον ἐν πάσῃ ἀσφαλείᾳ καὶ τοὺς φύλακας ἑστῶτας ἐπὶ τῶν θυρῶν ἀνοίξαντες δὲ ἔσω οὐδένα εὕρομεν

passages.text: When the captain of the temple guard and the chief priests heard this account, they were perplexed as to what was happening.
passages.sermon:
The captain of the temple guard heard the report.
The chief priests also heard the report.
They did not understand what was happening.
They were confused about the situation.
passages.original: Ὡς δὲ ἤκουσαν τοὺς λόγους τούτους ὅ τε στρατηγὸς τοῦ ἱεροῦ καὶ οἱ ἀρχιερεῖς διηπόρουν περὶ αὐτῶν τί ἂν γένοιτο τοῦτο

passages.text: Then someone came in and announced, “Look, the men you put in jail are standing in the temple courts teaching the people!”
passages.sermon:
A man arrived.
He spoke to the leaders.
He gave them news.
He said, “Look!”
He said, “The men you put in jail are in the temple courts.”
He said, “They are standing there.”
He said, “They are teaching the people.”
passages.original: παραγενόμενος δέ τις ἀπήγγειλεν αὐτοῖς ὅτι Ἰδοὺ οἱ ἄνδρες οὓς ἔθεσθε ἐν τῇ φυλακῇ εἰσὶν ἐν τῷ ἱερῷ ἑστῶτες καὶ διδάσκοντες τὸν λαόν

passages.text: At that point, the captain went with the officers and brought the apostles—but not by force, for fear the people would stone them.
passages.sermon:
The captain led the officers.
The captain and the officers went to the apostles.
They brought the apostles with them.
They did not use force.
They feared the people.
They thought the people might stone them.
passages.original: Τότε ἀπελθὼν ὁ στρατηγὸς σὺν τοῖς ὑπηρέταις ἦγεν αὐτούς οὐ μετὰ βίας ἐφοβοῦντο γὰρ τὸν λαόν μὴ λιθασθῶσιν

passages.text: They brought them in and made them stand before the Sanhedrin, where the high priest interrogated them.
passages.sermon:
The officers brought the apostles in.
The officers made the apostles stand before the Sanhedrin.
The Sanhedrin was the Jewish ruling council.
The high priest was present.
The high priest questioned the apostles.
passages.original: ἀγαγόντες δὲ αὐτοὺς ἔστησαν ἐν τῷ συνεδρίῳ καὶ ἐπηρώτησεν αὐτοὺς ὁ ἀρχιερεὺς

passages.text: “We gave you strict orders not to teach in this name,” he said. “Yet you have filled Jerusalem with your teaching and are determined to make us responsible for this man’s blood.”
passages.sermon:
The high priest spoke to the apostles.
He said, “We gave you strict orders.”
He said, “We told you not to teach in this name.”
He said, “But you have filled Jerusalem with your teaching.”
He said, “You want to make us responsible for this man’s blood.”
passages.original: λέγων Οὐ Παραγγελίᾳ παρηγγείλαμεν ὑμῖν μὴ διδάσκειν ἐπὶ τῷ ὀνόματι τούτῳ καὶ ἰδοὺ πεπληρώκατε τὴν Ἰερουσαλὴμ τῆς διδαχῆς ὑμῶν καὶ βούλεσθε ἐπαγαγεῖν ἐφ’ ἡμᾶς τὸ αἷμα τοῦ ἀνθρώπου τούτου

passages.text: But Peter and the other apostles replied, “We must obey God rather than men.
passages.sermon:
Peter was an apostle of Jesus.
Other apostles stood with Peter.
The high priest and the Sanhedrin questioned them.
Peter and the apostles answered the high priest.
They said, “We must obey God.
We must obey God more than we obey people.”
passages.original: Ἀποκριθεὶς δὲ Πέτρος καὶ οἱ ἀπόστολοι εἶπαν Πειθαρχεῖν δεῖ Θεῷ μᾶλλον ἢ ἀνθρώποις

passages.text: The God of our fathers raised up Jesus, whom you had killed by hanging Him on a tree.
passages.sermon:
The God of our fathers acted.
He raised up Jesus.
You killed Jesus.
You hung Jesus on a tree.
passages.original: ὁ Θεὸς τῶν πατέρων ἡμῶν ἤγειρεν Ἰησοῦν ὃν ὑμεῖς διεχειρίσασθε κρεμάσαντες ἐπὶ ξύλου

passages.text: God exalted Him to His right hand as Prince and Savior, in order to grant repentance and forgiveness of sins to Israel.
passages.sermon:
God raised Jesus to a place of highest honor.
God placed Jesus at His right hand.
God made Jesus Prince.
God made Jesus Savior.
God did this so that Israel could repent.
God did this so that Israel could receive forgiveness of sins.
passages.original: τοῦτον ὁ Θεὸς Ἀρχηγὸν καὶ Σωτῆρα ὕψωσεν τῇ δεξιᾷ αὐτοῦ τοῦ δοῦναι μετάνοιαν τῷ Ἰσραὴλ καὶ ἄφεσιν ἁμαρτιῶν

passages.text: We are witnesses of these things, and so is the Holy Spirit, whom God has given to those who obey Him.”
passages.sermon: We are witnesses of these things.\r\nThe Holy Spirit is also a witness.\r\nGod has given the Holy Spirit to those who obey Him.
passages.original: καὶ ἡμεῖς ἐσμεν μάρτυρες τῶν ῥημάτων τούτων καὶ τὸ Πνεῦμα τὸ Ἅγιον ὃ ἔδωκεν ὁ Θεὸς τοῖς πειθαρχοῦσιν αὐτῷ

passages.text: When the Council members heard this, they were enraged, and they resolved to put the apostles to death.
passages.sermon: The Council members heard this message.\r\nThey became very angry.\r\nThey decided to kill the apostles.
passages.original: Οἱ δὲ ἀκούσαντες διεπρίοντο καὶ ἐβουλεύοντο ἀνελεῖν αὐτούς

passages.text: But a Pharisee named Gamaliel, a teacher of the law who was honored by all the people, stood up in the Sanhedrin and ordered that the men be put outside for a short time.
passages.sermon:
Gamaliel was a Pharisee.
He was a teacher of the law.
All the people honored Gamaliel.
Gamaliel stood up in the Sanhedrin.
He ordered the men to be put outside for a short time.
passages.original: Ἀναστὰς δέ τις ἐν τῷ συνεδρίῳ Φαρισαῖος ὀνόματι Γαμαλιήλ νομοδιδάσκαλος τίμιος παντὶ τῷ λαῷ ἐκέλευσεν ἔξω βραχὺ τοὺς ἀνθρώπους ποιῆσαι

passages.text: “Men of Israel,” he said, “consider carefully what you are about to do to these men.
passages.sermon:
Gamaliel was a Pharisee.
He was a teacher of the law.
All the people honored him.
He stood up in the Sanhedrin.
He spoke to the Council members.
He said, “Men of Israel, pay attention.
Be careful about what you plan to do to these men.”
passages.original: Εἶπέν τε πρὸς αὐτούς Ἄνδρες Ἰσραηλῖται προσέχετε ἑαυτοῖς ἐπὶ τοῖς ἀνθρώποις τούτοις τί μέλλετε πράσσειν

passages.text: Some time ago Theudas rose up, claiming to be somebody, and about four hundred men joined him. He was killed, all his followers were dispersed, and it all came to nothing.
passages.sermon:
Theudas was a man who lived some time ago.
He claimed to be somebody important.
About four hundred men joined Theudas.
Someone killed Theudas.
All his followers scattered.
Their movement ended in nothing.
passages.original: πρὸ γὰρ τούτων τῶν ἡμερῶν ἀνέστη Θευδᾶς λέγων εἶναί τινα ἑαυτόν ᾧ προσεκλίθη ἀνδρῶν ἀριθμὸς ὡς τετρακοσίων ὃς ἀνῃρέθη καὶ πάντες ὅσοι ἐπείθοντο αὐτῷ διελύθησαν καὶ ἐγένοντο εἰς οὐδέν

passages.text: After him, Judas the Galilean appeared in the days of the census and drew away people after him. He too perished, and all his followers were scattered.
passages.sermon:
Judas the Galilean appeared after Theudas.
This happened during the days of the census.
Judas led people to follow him.
Judas died.
All who followed Judas were scattered.
passages.original: μετὰ τοῦτον ἀνέστη Ἰούδας ὁ Γαλιλαῖος ἐν ταῖς ἡμέραις τῆς ἀπογραφῆς καὶ ἀπέστησεν λαὸν ὀπίσω αὐτοῦ κἀκεῖνος ἀπώλετο καὶ πάντες ὅσοι ἐπείθοντο αὐτῷ διεσκορπίσθησαν

passages.text: So in the present case I advise you: Leave these men alone. Let them go! For if their purpose or endeavor is of human origin, it will fail.
passages.sermon:
Gamaliel was a respected teacher of the law.
He spoke to the Jewish council about the apostles.
He said, “Now I tell you this.
Stay away from these men.
Let them go.
If their plan or work comes from people,
it will fail.”
passages.original: Καὶ τὰ νῦν λέγω ὑμῖν ἀπόστητε ἀπὸ τῶν ἀνθρώπων τούτων καὶ ἄφετε αὐτούς ὅτι ἐὰν ᾖ ἐξ ἀνθρώπων ἡ βουλὴ αὕτη ἢ τὸ ἔργον τοῦτο καταλυθήσεται

passages.text: But if it is from God, you will not be able to stop them. You may even find yourselves fighting against God.”
passages.sermon:
Gamaliel was a respected teacher of the law.
He spoke to the Jewish council about the apostles.
He said, “If their work comes from God, you cannot stop them.
You will not be able to destroy them.
You may even find yourselves fighting against God.”
passages.original: εἰ δὲ ἐκ Θεοῦ ἐστιν οὐ δυνήσεσθε καταλῦσαι αὐτούς μή‿ ποτε καὶ θεομάχοι εὑρεθῆτε

passages.text: At this, they yielded to Gamaliel. They called the apostles in and had them flogged. Then they ordered them not to speak in the name of Jesus, and released them.
passages.sermon:
The Sanhedrin listened to Gamaliel.
They agreed with his advice.
They called the apostles to come in.
They flogged the apostles.
They commanded the apostles not to speak in the name of Jesus.
They released the apostles.
passages.original: Ἐπείσθησαν δὲ αὐτῷ καὶ προσκαλεσάμενοι τοὺς ἀποστόλους δείραντες παρήγγειλαν μὴ λαλεῖν ἐπὶ τῷ ὀνόματι τοῦ Ἰησοῦ καὶ ἀπέλυσαν

passages.text: The apostles left the Sanhedrin, rejoicing that they had been counted worthy of suffering disgrace for the Name.
passages.sermon:
The apostles left the Sanhedrin.
The Sanhedrin was the Jewish ruling council.
The apostles felt joy as they left.
They rejoiced because they suffered disgrace.
They suffered disgrace for the Name of Jesus.
They believed God counted them worthy to suffer for Jesus.
passages.original: Οἱ μὲν οὖν ἐπορεύοντο χαίροντες ἀπὸ προσώπου τοῦ συνεδρίου ὅτι κατηξιώθησαν ὑπὲρ τοῦ Ὀνόματος ἀτιμασθῆναι

passages.text: Every day, in the temple courts and from house to house, they did not stop teaching and proclaiming the good news that Jesus is the Christ.
passages.sermon:
The apostles followed Jesus Christ.
They taught and preached about Jesus every day.
They went to the temple courts every day.
They also went from house to house every day.
They did not stop teaching about Jesus.
They did not stop proclaiming the good news.
They declared that Jesus is the Christ.
passages.original: πᾶσάν τε ἡμέραν ἐν τῷ ἱερῷ καὶ κατ’ οἶκον οὐκ ἐπαύοντο διδάσκοντες καὶ εὐαγγελιζόμενοι τὸν Χριστὸν Ἰησοῦν
